topic: Function Overloading via Function Pointers and Virtual Dispatch in C
explanation: In advanced C programming, achieving polymorphic behavior similar to object-oriented languages requires leveraging function pointers and manual dispatch mechanisms. This technique allows different functions to be called based on the runtime type of an object, enabling dynamic behavior and simulating method overriding. It is used to implement flexible, extensible systems where behavior varies depending on object types without relying on language-level features like inheritance.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how to implement runtime polymorphism in C by embedding a function pointer within a base struct and assigning different function implementations depending on the derived type. When calling 'b->print_total', the function executed depends on the actual function pointer assigned, effectively overriding behavior. This technique is essential for advanced C programming to simulate object-oriented features like method overriding and dynamic dispatch, enabling flexible and extensible code architectures.
